text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY: HIGH - tenant Sable (tenant_id:sable-82) tail latency > 500ms for 5m, error-rate 1.4%. Trigger: tenant-tail-latency>500ms. Please ack.
jamal: acked. I'm taking this — oncall here. Any recent deploys to Dedicated pool-3?
suzanne: not aware of any deploys in the last 2h. CI shows last deploy 03:12 UTC ~1h ago.
maya: quick grep of logs shows a lot of long-running batches hitting `max_batch_tokens` in the scheduler. Spikes align with bursts in request rate when queue length > 120. suspect bespoke batching profile for Sable.
ryan-eng: confirmed — tenant config: `scheduler_profile: bespoke-sable-v2` with `max_batch_tokens: 2048`, `prefer_latency: false`. That allows very large batches; under bursty small-payload traffic it increases tail latency.
jamal: mitigation proposal: 1) reduce `max_batch_tokens` -> 512, 2) enable strict preemption (scheduler.knobs.preempt=true), 3) lower queue_weight for sable to 0.6 so other tenants can get throughput. Can we hotpatch?
suzanne: yes, we can hotpatch via infractl. Command: `infractl sched patch --tenant sable-82 --set max_batch_tokens=512 --set preempt=true --set queue_weight=0.6` — should propagate config to all replicas in pool within ~15s.
ops-bot: rolling update initiated for tenant sable-82 on pool dedicated-3 (replicas: 6).
jamal: applying now.
jamal: ```
infractl sched patch --tenant sable-82 --set max_batch_tokens=512 --set preempt=true --set queue_weight=0.6
```
ops-bot: patch applied on 6 nodes. Reconfig broadcast complete.
maya: watching metrics — tail latency (99th) dropping: 630ms -> 190ms in the first 45s post-patch. error-rate down to 0.3%.
cust-success-eli: DM-ing Sable contacts: "We applied a hotfix to reduce batch size and adjust queue weights. You should see latency improvements; we're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem." They replied: "Thanks, big improvement so far"
ryan-eng: note — smaller batches will increase per-token compute overhead; flagging to Cost dashboard: `dash://tenants/sable-82/cost` and billing watch.
jamal: filing incident ticket INC-2024-4235, severity P2. Root cause hypothesis: bespoke `max_batch_tokens` set too large for tenant's bursty small-request workload. Immediate mitigation: reduced `max_batch_tokens`, enabled preemption, lowered queue weight to limit ramping.
suzanne: adding rollback snippet to ticket (if needed):
```
# rollback to pre-incident values
infractl sched patch --tenant sable-82 --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set preempt=false --set queue_weight=1.0
```
jamal: setting monitoring suppression for the tenant-tail-latency alert for 30m while we observe.
ops-bot: alert suppression in place (30m) for rule tenant-tail-latency for tenant sable-82.
maya: handing off monitoring to night oncall (me) in 10m — current state stable, 95th/99th ~150-210ms. I'll escalate if it drifts back above 400ms.
cust-success-eli: customer asked for ETA on a postmortem. I told them we'll share a preliminary timeline within 24h.
ryan-eng: follow-up actions: 1) re-evaluate bespoke-sable-v2 profile heuristics (max_batch_tokens adaptive?), 2) run synthetic replay against dedicated-3 with small-payload bursts to validate, 3) add a guardrail alert for per-tenant max_batch_tokens growth vs median payload size.
jamal: thanks all. Handoff notes written into INC-2024-4235 with the exact infractl commands, metrics snapshot, and customer comms. Last message here.
